question.text: Part C of the Schedule to the PMLA 2002 covers which type of offences?

answer.text: Only offences committed by foreign nationals in India
Only offences committed within the territory of India
Offences with cross-border implications specified in Part A, offences against property under Chapter XVII of the IPC, and section 51 Black Money Act tax/penalty/interest evasion offences
Only offences related to narcotics and psychotropic substances

explanation.text: The Logic: Part C of the Schedule to the PMLA covers (i) offences with cross-border implications specified in Part A, (ii) offences against property under Chapter XVII of the Indian Penal Code, and (iii) the wilful attempt to evade tax, penalty or interest under section 51 of the Black Money Act, 2015. The Trap: Part C is not limited to foreign nationals, not limited to offences committed only in India, and not limited to narcotics offences. Its scope is driven by cross-border implications and the specific Black Money Act limb. Note: Cross-border implications run in both directions — offences committed abroad with proceeds coming to India, and offences committed in India with proceeds going abroad.
